chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them) that they said:
"You only receive from your prayer what you were attentive to in it; if you were heedless of all of it or neglected its performance, it will be rolled up and struck against the face of its owner."
ai.seo_question: What happens to prayer if one is completely heedless during it?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on forgetfulness (sahw) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the Shia emphasis on *khushu'* (attentiveness) as the essence of prayer's validity, rather than mere mechanical performance. The metaphor of the prayer being 'rolled up' and struck against the face illustrates the spiritual consequence of total heedlessness, a concept deeply rooted in the Imams' teachings on the quality of worship. It serves as a practical reminder for believers to cultivate mindfulness even during routine prayers to ensure their acceptance.
